measures.what_it_does: Authorizes a one-year excess property tax for the Columbia County Park and Recreation Pool District in 2026, collected in 2027, to operate the district and maintain the pool it plans to build in Dayton (the old Dayton pool closed in 2017). The district, formed by voters in 2023, covers the county except the Town of Starbuck and the Prescott park district's area; voters approved the same levy in 2024 and 2025.
measures.cost_line: $200,000 collected in 2027, approximately $0.20 per $1,000 of assessed value (about $60 a year on a $300,000 home, by the Union-Bulletin's estimate).
measures.pro_summary: The statement for, by Kevin Rust, says the planned 'modest pool' would offer swim lessons that 'help curb drowning,' summer jobs, a competition-size pool and therapy swims, and that the commissioners have secured grants and donations for construction; a yes vote 'secures funding for operation and maintenance, which is voted on annually.'
measures.con_summary: No statement against was submitted. In November 2025, 39.8% of voters (564 of 1,418) voted no on the same levy.

taxes.basis: A yes vote continues an excess levy of about $0.20 per $1,000 that voters approved for 2025 and 2026 collection, at the same amount, so it maps at the renewal tier (+1).

measures.sources_note: Columbia County local voters' pamphlet PDF p. 10 (S1); VoteWA guide record 7423 (S2); sample ballot (S3); Union-Bulletin coverage of the 2026 levy (S4), the 2024 levy (S5, S6) and its tax effect (S7); SOS results for the 2023 formation and the 2024 and 2025 levies (S8-S10).

measures.what_it_does: Authorizes a one-year excess property tax for the Prescott Joint Park and Recreation District's maintenance and operation in 2027, its main source of operating money, chiefly for the Prescott community pool. The district is joint with Walla Walla County; in Columbia County only a thinly settled western strip is in it. The November 2025 request failed, missing the 60% it needed by less than half a percent.
measures.cost_line: $175,000 collected in 2027 across the whole district, approximately $0.35 per $1,000 of assessed value (about $70 a year on a $200,000 home, by the Union-Bulletin's 2025 estimate at the same rate).
measures.pro_summary: The statement for, by Hailey Hudson and Debby Phillips, says the pool is where kids learn to swim and teenagers find summer jobs, that without the pool this summer families had to drive to other towns for swim lessons, and that 'once a community pool is gone, it's incredibly difficult to bring it back.'
measures.con_summary: No statement against was submitted and no opposition committee was named. The same amount fell just short of 60% in November 2025; Columbia County's part voted 3 yes, 1 no.

taxes.basis: A yes vote imposes a $175,000 excess levy (about $0.35 per $1,000) for 2027. After the 2025 levy failed, no excess levy is in place to renew, so approval restarts the tax at an amount above the $145,000 last approved.

measures.sources_note: Columbia County local voters' pamphlet PDF p. 11 (S1); VoteWA guide record 7379 (S2); Union-Bulletin coverage of the 2025 levy and its failure (S3, S4); SOS Columbia County precinct results for 2025 (S5), 2022 (S6) and 2024 (S7).
